title: The Tenth Doctor
description: Portrayed by David Tennant, this incarnation of the Doctor is a Time Lord from Gallifrey. He travels in the TARDIS with companions including Rose Tyler and Martha Jones, faces the Master, and encounters River Song for the first time in his personal timeline.

title: Ruby Sunday
description: Ruby is a musician raised by her adoptive mother Carla and grandmother Cherry. After meeting the Doctor during a Christmas encounter with goblins, she joins him in the TARDIS. Her search for her birth mother forms a central part of her story.

title: Rose Tyler
description: Rose works in a London department store before an encounter with the Autons brings her into the Doctor's life. She travels with the Ninth and Tenth Doctors and later works to cross the barrier between parallel worlds when the universe is threatened.

title: Martha Jones
description: Martha is studying medicine when the hospital where she works is transported to the Moon. Her courage earns her an invitation to travel with the Doctor. When the Master captures him, Martha travels across Earth to spread a story of resistance.

title: River Song
description: River Song is an archaeologist whose encounters with the Doctor do not unfold in the same order for both of them. Her identity as Melody Pond, daughter of Amy and Rory, connects her personal history to the Doctor's adventures. Alex Kingston portrays her.

title: The companion changes the journey
description: Why Doctor Who's human travellers offer several different ways into the same extraordinary universe.
imageAlt: Official Doctor Who Season 2 trailer thumbnail
body: A machine that can travel through time and space seems to promise an unlimited number of stories. Doctor Who's companions give those stories a point of view. Rose, Martha and Ruby each arrive with a life that exists before the TARDIS. River complicates the order in which a life is revealed. Reading their official profiles together suggests an approachable way to explore a long-running television world: begin with a person whose questions interest you, then follow the adventures around them. This commentary contains broad character spoilers.

Rose's first encounter with the Doctor interrupts an ordinary working day. That contrast is useful for a new viewer because the extraordinary does not need to begin in an extraordinary setting. Her profile traces a shop assistant into travels with the Doctor and later into efforts to bridge parallel worlds. The appeal of that outline is the changing scale of her agency. The person being introduced to danger can become a person who actively responds to it.

Martha arrives with medical training and a practical response to crisis. Her hospital's journey to the Moon is spectacular, but the official profile emphasizes her bravery and later her work carrying a story of resistance across Earth. One way to read this is that knowledge and communication deserve space beside gadgets and confrontations. It also makes a useful viewing question: when a scene becomes chaotic, which character notices what another person needs?

Ruby brings music, an adoptive family and questions about her origins into her travels. Those details give the viewer connections beyond the next alien encounter. River, in contrast, asks us to pay attention to chronology itself. Her encounters with the Doctor unfold in different orders for each of them. A timeline can therefore clarify facts, but it cannot replace the experience of learning something at a particular moment in a story.

The Tenth Doctor's profile sits alongside these human perspectives rather than cancelling them out. His ability to travel is the premise; the people who travel with him help shape what a journey means. For a manageable starting exercise, choose one companion profile and one official episode link from its source. Record what the character knows at the beginning and what they choose by the end. This is an interpretation exercise rather than an official watch order, and it works without treating decades of television as homework that must be completed first.
